Where are you moving?

Two ZIP codes give us the distance and the type of move.

Estimator's noteShort moves are usually billed by the hour for the crew and truck. Long moves are priced by the weight of your things and the distance. Your ZIP codes decide which applies.

Your price shows before we ask for any contact details.

A moving company costs $380–$960 to move a 1-bedroom home across town and $1,150–$2,850 for a 3-bedroom house, for 10 road miles on an off-peak date with no stairs and no add-ons. That is how much does a moving company cost when it bills by the hour for a crew and a truck. Sent 1,000 road miles instead, the same 3-bedroom house costs $4,000–$8,550, priced on weight and distance.

What goes into a moving company's price

A quote can look like one number, but how much does a moving company cost is really the sum of several charges. Knowing them lets you read a quote line by line and spot what one company includes and another leaves out until moving day.

  • Labor. The movers' time on a local job, or the weight they load and haul on a long one. This is the largest share of how much does a moving company cost on most jobs.
  • The truck and fuel. Local companies usually fold the truck into the hourly rate. Long-distance companies often add a fuel surcharge that follows diesel prices.
  • Travel time or a trip fee. Many local movers bill the drive from their depot to your door and back, either as clock time or as a flat trip charge.
  • Packing and materials. Boxes, tape, wrap and the labor to pack them are billed on top when the crew packs for you.
  • Access charges. Flights of stairs, a long carry from the door to the truck, an elevator, or a shuttle truck for streets a large truck can't reach.
  • Heavy or delicate items. A safe, a grand piano or a hot tub needs extra hands or equipment and gets its own line.
  • Valuation and storage. Extra liability cover and any days your things spend in a warehouse are priced separately.

Two quotes for the same home can differ by hundreds of dollars only because one includes travel time, materials or a fuel charge and the other adds them to the final bill. Ask each company to put every charge in writing, so how much does a moving company cost on paper matches what you pay.

How much does a moving company cost across town?

Local moving companies charge by the hour, so how much does a moving company cost across town is the crew's hourly rate times the hours on the job. The rate covers the movers and the truck, and it climbs with each mover the job needs.

A 1-bedroom home usually takes 2 movers, whose rate together is $100–$150 an hour, or $50–$75 an hour for each mover with the truck. The whole move costs $380–$960 at 10 road miles, off peak, with no stairs or add-ons. A 3-bedroom house usually takes 4 movers at $200–$300 an hour together, and the move costs $1,150–$2,850 on the same terms. The crew table below shows how the hours and the total change as you add or drop a mover.

Before you book a local company, ask three things that change the hourly bill: whether there is a minimum number of hours, whether the clock starts at the depot or at your door, and whether time is billed in full hours or in smaller blocks. A company with a lower rate and a high minimum can cost more on a small job than one with a higher rate and no minimum. Those three answers can change how much does a moving company cost more than a small gap between two hourly rates.

Moving company prices over long distances

For a move of hundreds of miles, or any move across a state line, how much does a moving company cost depends on the weight or volume of your shipment and the distance, not on hours. The company estimates the weight from an inventory of your home, or weighs the truck before and after loading.

A 3-bedroom house moved 1,000 road miles costs $4,000–$8,550, off peak, with no stairs and no add-ons, which works out to about $4.04–$8.50 per mile. That per-mile figure is the total spread over the distance, not a rate movers quote. A 1-bedroom home on the same route costs $1,400–$3,300.

An interstate mover must give you a written estimate. A binding estimate fixes the price for the items and services it lists, while a non-binding one can change with the actual weight, within a federal limit. FMCSA explains how each kind of estimate works. Long-distance companies also deliver within a window of days rather than on a set date, so get the window in writing with the price.

Full service, partial service or labor only

How much does a moving company cost also depends on how much of the work you hand over. Most companies sell the same move at three levels of service:

  • Full service. The crew packs, loads, drives, unloads and can unpack. It costs the most and saves you the most time.
  • Move only. You pack every box, and the company loads, drives and unloads. The prices on this page are for this level.
  • Labor only. You rent the truck, and a crew loads it, unloads it, or both. You drive.

The comparison below prices your move with movers, a rental truck and a portable container, and the truck guide shows which size a self-drive move needs. If you pack yourself, the box estimator further down counts the boxes, tape and paper room by room, so you can weigh them against the packing charge. Packing yourself is the simplest way to cut how much does a moving company cost without changing companies.

Carriers, van lines and brokers

The company you call is not always the one that moves you. A local mover runs its own crews and trucks. A national van line books moves through local agents, who pack and load under the van line's name. A broker sells the move and hands it to a carrier, and owns no trucks. Each model can work, but a broker's price is only as firm as the carrier that takes the job.

For a move across state lines, look up the company's USDOT number before you sign. FMCSA's records show whether it is registered as a carrier or a broker, and its guide to choosing a mover lists what else to check. Federal rules also require an interstate mover to give you the booklet Your Rights and Responsibilities When You Move. Knowing who will turn up is part of knowing how much does a moving company cost, since a carrier that never saw your home may re-price the job when it arrives.

Charges that raise a moving company's bill

The prices above assume an easy job. These details push how much does a moving company cost toward the top of its range, or past it:

  • Peak dates. Summer, weekends and the last days of the month are when moving companies are busiest. In the rate table behind the calculator, a July date raises both ends of the range for the same home and distance.
  • Stairs and long carries. Full flights of stairs, a walk of more than about 75 feet from the door to the truck, or a booked elevator add time or a fee.
  • A shuttle. Where a full-size truck can't reach your door, the company moves your things to a smaller truck and bills for the extra handling.
  • Bulky items. A gun safe, a pool table or a piano needs extra hands, a dolly or a crane.
  • Waiting time. If the crew waits for keys, an elevator or a home that isn't packed, the hourly clock keeps running.

Tips and liability cover sit outside the quote. The tip calculator below works out what tipping guides suggest for your crew, and the valuation panel shows what each level of cover pays if something breaks.

Checking how much does a moving company cost before you book

An online figure stays a range until a company has seen your home. To turn it into a price you can hold a company to:

  1. Run your ZIP codes and home size through the calculator above. It's free, takes about a minute and needs no email to show your range.
  2. Ask at least three companies for a written estimate after an in-home or video walk-through, and give each the same list of rooms, items and services.
  3. Line the estimates up charge by charge: crew size and hours or weight, travel time, materials, access fees and valuation.
  4. Work through the checklist below in the weeks before moving day, from reading reviews to photographing valuables, so the crew's paid time goes on moving.

A written estimate far below the calculator's range deserves a question before you pay a deposit. Hold every company's figure against your own estimate, and you will know how much does a moving company cost for your home before anyone carries a box.

  • Long-distance companies price by the weight of your shipment and the miles it travels.
  • Travel time, fuel, materials and access fees can sit outside a quote, so ask for every charge in writing.
  • Check whether you're dealing with a carrier or a broker before you pay a deposit.

Vetting the company and getting ready for the crew

Part of how much does a moving company cost on the day is set weeks before it. These tasks run from reading reviews and checking the company to clearing a path, so the crew never waits.

0 of 14 done

8 weeks before

  • Paper or digital, keep every page a company gives you until the move is settled.

  • Look at how each one handled problems, not only at the star rating.

6 weeks before

  • Moving hours, elevators, loading docks and gates. If one wants the company's certificate of insurance, ask the company to send it ahead.

  • Then compare it with the coverage the moving company offers.

4 weeks before

  • Keys, documents, medicine, chargers and anything you can't replace.

  • Get close-ups of any damage that's already there, so a claim later is clear.

2 weeks before

  • Give them the new address and the date you move.

  • Government agencies and financial institutions don't allow forwarding of sensitive mail such as driver's licenses, bank statements and credit cards, so tell each one yourself.

1 week before

  • The truck may block a driveway or part of the street for a while.

The day before

  • Take up rugs that slide, and protect floors where heavy pieces will roll.

Moving day

  • Note any damage on the paperwork before you sign for delivery.

  • Point out anything fragile, very heavy or going to a particular room.

After the move

  • Say what went well and what didn't; it helps the next person choosing.

What to tip a moving company's crew

Tips are not part of how much does a moving company cost in a quote. This works out what published tipping guides suggest for each mover and for the whole crew, by the length of the job.

3 movers 4–6.5 hours

Per mover $16–$98

For the crew $48–$294

Who to tip and when

  • Tipping is up to you: guides call a tip a thank-you for good work, not an obligation. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides find cash simplest, handed to each mover at the end of the job. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House, MoveAdvisor and CNET)
  • When one crew loads and another unloads, guides suggest tipping each crew after it finishes its part. (HireAHelper, CNET, Real Simple, American Van Lines and NerdWallet)
  • On a move of several days, guides suggest tipping at the end of each day, in case the crew changes. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet and Forbes Home)
  • Guides suggest a separate tip for a separate packing crew. (CNET and This Old House)
  • Guides suggest asking the moving company about its tipping policy first: some build gratuity into the price, and some don't accept tips. (Forbes Home, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides suggest tipping more for stairs, heavy furniture or bad weather, and less, or nothing, for damage, a late start or careless work. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, CNET and Real Simple)
  • Drinks and snacks are welcome, but guides don't count them as the tip. (NerdWallet and CNET)

What the company pays if something breaks

Interstate moving companies offer two levels of liability. See what basic released value pays for a damaged item against full-value protection, so you know what a quote actually covers.

If your $400 TV is broken, basic cover pays $36.

Released value, the basic cover a mover includes at no charge, pays at most 60 cents a pound for each item. Full-value protection pays to repair or replace it, up to its value. The released rate is the Surface Transportation Board's, and a mover may raise it each year. Full-value protection is the default: a mover's estimate must include it, and your goods move under it unless you give it up in writing. Under it, a mover may pay at most $100 a pound for an item worth more than $100 a pound, such as jewelry, unless you list the item in writing.

Released value pays $36

Full-value protection pays up to $400

Full-value protection is priced on the whole shipment: about $10.00–$20.00 per $1,000 of declared value.

Questions

How much does a moving company cost for your move? FAQ

Can't find your answer? Email hello@liftmyboxes.com.

How much does a moving company cost to move a 2,000 sq ft house?

A 2,000 sq ft house usually has about 3 bedrooms, so a local move costs $1,150–$2,850 for 10 road miles, off peak, with no stairs or add-ons. Moved 1,000 road miles, it costs $4,000–$8,550. A full basement, a packed garage or heavy furniture can push how much does a moving company cost above those ranges.

How much should you set aside beyond the moving company's bill?

Plan for what the quote leaves out: tips, packing supplies if you pack yourself, cleaning, utility deposits, and travel or a hotel night on a long move. On an interstate move, add full-value protection if the price includes only basic released value. A cushion on top of how much does a moving company cost also covers access fees that only show up on moving day.

Do moving companies charge a minimum number of hours?

Many local companies do, often two to four hours, and some add a trip fee for the drive to your home. On a small job the minimum can matter more than the hourly rate, because you pay for it even if the crew finishes early. Ask for the minimum and the travel policy in writing.

Can you hire a moving company without its truck?

Yes. Many companies sell labor only: a crew loads or unloads a truck or container you rent, and you drive. It costs less than a full-service move because the company supplies no truck and no driver. The comparison on this page can add loading help to the rental-truck price, so you can set it beside a full-service crew.

Is a moving company's quote the final price?

Not always. On a local hourly move, the final bill follows the hours the crew actually works, plus any fees for access or extra services. On an interstate move, ask whether the written estimate is binding or non-binding before you compare how much does a moving company cost from one company to the next.
